newsitem.title: USA: Florida counties seen relying more on user fees.
newsitem.headline: Florida counties seen relying more on user fees.

text.p: Florida counties will increasingly be forced to levy user fees to fund services for their growing populations, the president of the Florida Association of Counties predicted.
FAC president Carol Roberts, a Palm Beach County commissioner, told the Bond Buyer's Florida Public Finance Conference that Florida continues to gain 900 new residents daily.
"The explosive growth that Florida experienced over the last century certainly is not stopping," Roberts said.
Income taxes are prohibited in Florida, and many of the state's 67 counties are already at or near Florida's constitutional 10 mill limit on ad valorem taxes.
With decreasing revenue sources, bonding is not an option for those counties," Roberts said.

At the same time, 13 poor, rural Florida counties have no ad valorem tax revenues because the assessed value of their properties all fall below the state's $25,000 homestead exemption for property taxes, said Roberts. Those counties are struggling to extend services to newly settled areas because they receive no new tax revenues when additional low-cost housing is built.
"User fees are a fairer way to operate," Roberts said. "Many counties are going to have to look at fees. I believe more smaller and more large counties will adopt that formula."
